items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: she trained me to be her assistant at the church, and then I used to play for her at Sunday school. I became the Sunday school pianist.

ctx.x: at the time, very small, and this was so marvelous, because at the time we had a woman in Lake Charles who was -- I can't remember her maiden name, but her name was Mrs. Alton J. Foster, who was also a very magnificent concert pianist. Her husband at one time I think was the President of the rice mill up there, if I'm not mistaken. And she happened to have been at this particular event and she was very inspired by me, and she contacted my teacher and she told her she would like her to bring me down to her home,…

But anyway, Mrs. Eugenia Reynaud was also the organist and the pianist of the little Baptist Church where we belonged, the Sunlight Baptist Church in Lake Charles. And she trained me to be her assistant at the church, and then I used to play for her at Sunday school. I became the Sunday school pianist. I was getting the big sum of $2.00 a month. And when I would

help her, she would always give me, I think I'd get about four or five dollars for helping her with the music. So you know, after she had trained me I could carry on myself, so many Sundays when she couldn't come to church, if she felt ill, she felt like Nellie could carry on, so she would just let Nellie carry on, and I did. Of course the only thing was they used to have to wake me up at night to play for collection, you know, when it came time, after the minister had preached. Well, of course in those days -- I…
